To find the rank of $B,$ we first reduce it to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}B & =[\begin{aligned}6 & 9 & 3 \\ -2 & -2 & -1 \\ 12 & 18 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & 9 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 12 & 18 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & 9 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix has $2$ pivot columns (or alternatively, it has exactly $2$ non-zero rows).

Therefore, $\text{rank}(B)=2.$
